lines.text: What if you could drive from Russia to Alaska, over the sea?
Here at the Bering Strait, only 82 kilometres of sea separate them.
On a flat world map, they sit at opposite edges. Spin the map around the globe, and they nearly touch.
And right in the middle sit two islands: Big Diomede, which is Russian, and Little Diomede, which is American.
They're just 3.8 kilometres apart, and the sea around them is only 90 metres at its deepest. So why not a road?
So build it: one span from Russia to Big Diomede, a short hop to Little Diomede, and one more to Alaska. Three spans, and two continents are joined.
Now drive it. How far would that take you? From London, east across Europe, all through Siberia, over the bridge, then down through Alaska and Canada to New York.
Has anyone tried? Russia backed a plan: a 103 kilometre tunnel under the strait, priced at about $65B. It was never built.
And the strangest part: the International Date Line runs between the two islands. Drive east from Big Diomede, and you arrive in yesterday. A short drive apart, but almost a whole day apart in time.
Bridge or tunnel: which would you build? Either way, you could drive from Russia to Alaska.
